title: Principality of Drutsk
capsule: The Principality of Drutsk was a minor appanage carved from the Principality of Polotsk, centred on the fortress town of Druts (modern Belarus) on the Drut River, and first recorded as a distinct princely seat around 1111. It was ruled by a junior branch of the Polotsk Rurikids and never controlled substantial territory or trade routes of strategic importance. By the mid-thirteenth century the principality had been reabsorbed into the Polotsk sphere before the entire region fell under Lithuanian overlordship, with the Mongol destruction of Rus' lands after 1240 further erasing its political structures.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is poorly attested; the principality appears only incidentally in Rus' chronicles and no dedicated cartographic delimitation survives from the medieval period.
